h: The Three Shabbos Meals Cultivate Fear Service and Attachment

p: In Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma on this parsha (Bamidbar Rabbah 22:1):
"The Holy One, blessed be He, said
'You shall fear Hashem your God,' etc.;
'and to Him shall you cleave,' etc."
are in the holiness of Shabbos.
for the entire day of Shabbos
a person is full of fear and dread
in the prohibition of desecrating Shabbos;
these are those who keep Shabbos."
for on the day of Shabbos
except the service of Hashem Yisbarach.
For it is found in the Sifrei
that even thinking about work is forbidden on Shabbos.
it is found in the holy Zohar
and not a day of the body."
and he has no work on Shabbos
except the service of the day of souls,
that is, only the service of Hashem,
for the entire aim of the words of Torah
as is found in the holy Zohar
"And they went three days in the wilderness
the Torah had not been given to them!
אֵין תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
'Torah' means only the Holy One, blessed be He."
That is, the aim of the whole Torah
is to cleave to the Holy One, blessed be He.
only to occupy themselves with Torah";
that the Torah was given to Yisrael on Shabbos."
that he cleave to Torah scholars
and benefit them from his possessions,
and through this he will merit
allude to the three meals of Shabbos,
On the night of holy Shabbos,
the meal of the Field of holy apples,
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which corresponds to Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him
it corresponds to "and Him shall you serve";
for at the time of the Akeidah
and when the Holy One, blessed be He,
and he had no other occupation
except the service of Hashem all his days.
may allude to the morning meal,
which corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him;
for it is found in the Midrash on this parsha:
For there are levels in the fear of Hashem;
who prayed for the Men of the Great Assembly
to the prayer of Your servants
who desire to fear Your Name"
he called them only "desiring to fear."
And King Shlomo, peace be upon him, said (Mishlei 2:4-5):
and search for it like hidden treasures,
then you will understand the fear of Hashem"
רַק יָבִין מַה הוּא יִרְאַת ה׳
he will only understand what the fear of Hashem is.
implies that it is already fixed in him
and it is fitting to call him
for he is complete in his fear
And Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
was proven at the time of the Akeidah
to be clear in the fear of Hashem
For when he went to the Akeidah,
and to stop him from fulfilling the mitzvah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה נו, ד)
as is written in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 56:4):
You are a shedder of blood, etc.";
and that this was not a command from Hashem,
that he not offer him as an offering;
from which it would appear to Avraham
that he was going to act against the will of Him,
blessed be His Name, Heaven forbid.
And were it not for the dread of Hashem,
he could almost have been enticed;
only his fear stood by him.
And this is the aspect of fear
in which you are a fool
"and He will guard your foot from being caught."
And this is the intent of the Midrash cited above:
which corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
